main_text.l: quia, vel turpis, vel ἀδύνατος, aut falte diff-
icilis: vel denique detrimento sia ei qui ad nos
scribit. vbi satisfacere amici petitioni pla-
çuerit, poëlicitatio adhibenda erit studij &
officij noftri, eiusdem ratiōnes atq; cautelæ
adferendæ: quod nimirum res illa, quæ
petitur, cum honestate fit, vel utilitate
cōiuncta: neque vsque adeò ardua & diffici-
lis: is qui petit, de nobis aut nostris meri-
tis præclarè: ea præditus pietate, doctrina,
virtute, vt denegare ei nihil posfimus.
Quod si vero id quod petit amicus impro-
bare, aut non posse nos facere, oftendere
voluerimus: iifdem ex locis rationes ad-
ferendæ erunt contrariæ: & indicandum
gratificari ea in re amico nos non posse:
quod sit, aut turpis illa, aut perniciosa,
aut minus necessaria: aut difficilis, & impe-
dimenta multa magnaque obiiciantur,
quæ à personis, locis, temporibus fumen-
da. Refellenda quoque argumenta hîc e-
runt in petitione ab amico adhibita, vel
negando, vel exrenuando, vel compensan-
do, & docendum, commodum, verbi gra-
tia, nullum hîc esse: aut non esse tantum,
quantum existimetur: aut plura, altera ex
parte, damnasecum atque incommoda
adferre. Quemadmodum vero sententiæ

page.notes: Marginal note in the right margin, in small italic type, read as: "Sententia vsurpanda cum impro-banda aut denegandâ petitio." Printed lines were partly indistinct; the note's last words are approximate. Printed spelling ("aut", "vt", "sententiæ") kept as seen. The Greek word "ἀδύνατος" in the first line is a reading of the small Greek on the scan and may be imprecise. Some words near the bottom of the text ("damnasecum", "exrenuando", "compensando") are blurred and marked as printed; the page is also marked by show-through and a slight shadow at the left.
